note: Initial source-policy set (Step 01.4, I06), accepted by the product owner on 2026-09-25; web_public_pages and youtube moved to version 2 on 2026-09-28 (D28). Conservative defaults: a family that needs an agreement we do not have is blocked. These are engineering defaults, not legal advice; each new host or platform is still checked against its current terms. A change is a new policy_version. Loaded into ai_source_policies by a seed script at Step 03; code never hard-codes them. 29 Sep 2026: competitor_portals added and web_public_pages moved to version 3 (D34). From Step 05 these are loaded into ai_source_policies by `make seed`. 1 Oct 2026: web_public_pages v5, competitor_portals v2 and official_records v2 record robots.txt without enforcing it (D46). Step 06: spoken_video_content v2 and youtube v3 (D47). spoken_video_content v3 adds frames (D49).

conditions: Public pages only; never bypass login, paywall, CAPTCHA, rate limits or private groups
Allow-listed hosts only; a host is added by a recorded decision
Excluded hosts are governed by their own family policy
Minimum author metadata; no cross-platform profiles
Reviews quote one author's words with a credit line (platform and date); findings stay paraphrased and attributed
robots.txt is asked for every page and its verdict recorded; it does not block the fetch (D46)
policies.basis: docs/06 scraping policy. Version 2 (product owner, 28 Sep 2026, D28): reviews may quote the author's words with a credit line naming the platform and date; no link required. Each host's terms are still reviewed when it is added to the allow-list. Version 3 (28 Sep 2026, D34): competitor property portals are governed by their own family, competitor_portals, so their hosts are excluded here; rights are unchanged. Version 4 (product owner, 29 Sep 2026): first allow-list, chosen from a live Brave discovery for the five projects. Allowed: developer official sites (dlf.in, conscient.in, sobha.com, m3mindia.com), news sites (republicworld.com, thehindubusinessline.com, smestreet.in, constrofacilitator.com, nenow.in, propesatatenews.com) and 52 broker and marketing microsites. Left out: client-site.example (own content, not independent evidence), press-release wires (openpr.com, pninews.com) and unrelated sites. Developer and broker pages are marketing claims, not independent reviews. Version 5 (product owner, 1 Oct 2026, D46): robots.txt is recorded, not enforced. Pages that refuse our crawler are still not worked around (D33).

conditions: Public pages only; never sign in, use accounts or cookies, or pass a paywall

A page that refuses the web reader (401, 403, 406, 451) is asked for once more through Scrapfly's unblocker and residential proxies (D60), up to UNBLOCKED_PAGES_PER_RUN pages per collection job, within the shared Scrapfly credit ledger
User reviews are quoted in the author's words per D28, with a credit line naming the portal and date; no rewording
Minimum author metadata; no cross-platform profiles
Legal check recommended before any public release of quoted portal reviews
robots.txt is asked for every page and its verdict recorded; it does not block the fetch (D46)
policies.basis: D34 (product owner, 28 Sep 2026): user reviews on competitor portals may be collected, analysed and quoted with a credit line; the product owner accepts the copyright and terms risk. On 28 Sep 2026 99acres and Housing.com refused automated requests and MagicBricks disallows project pages for general crawlers; those limits are respected. Version 2 (product owner, 1 Oct 2026, D46): robots.txt is recorded, not enforced. Pages that refuse our crawler are still not worked around (D33). Version 3 (product owner, 13 Oct 2026, D60: "we need to scrap the data from the competitors as well"): refused pages are read through Scrapfly's unblocker; the product owner accepts the portals' terms-of-service risk, as for Instagram (D54).

conditions: Video and Short metadata and comments through the YouTube Data API
Captions and audio for transcription are governed by spoken_video_content, not this family (D33, D47)
Comments are separate sources attributed to the commenter, never to the creator
Titles, descriptions and metadata never count as spoken-content evidence
Quoted comments and spoken reviews are re-checked on refresh and withdrawn if removed
policies.basis: Conservative 30-day retention pending review of the YouTube API Services terms. Version 2 (product owner, 28 Sep 2026, D28): comments and authorised spoken content may be quoted as reviews with a credit line; published quotes are re-checked on every refresh and withdrawn if the comment or video is removed. Version 3 (Step 06, D47): the 'no downloading' condition moves to spoken_video_content, which governs captions and audio under D33; rights and retention unchanged.
policies.accepted_by: Product owner (D33, 28 Sep 2026; applied at Step 06)

conditions: Public videos only, and only videos linked to a catalogue project
Captions first (youtube-transcript-api); otherwise the video (480p or lower) through yt-dlp, for speech-to-text and sampled frames (D33)
No sign-in, cookies, proxies or bot-check workarounds; a refusal or a bot check stops the attempt and is recorded
Video and audio are deleted after each job; frames are never stored, shared or republished
Frames are read for on-screen text and visible facts only; people are not identified
Renders, graphics and undated footage never prove construction status; frame observations carry the video's date
Transcripts keep the original timing and language; translations are stored separately
Speech is attributed to the video with the speaker unknown unless the platform states it; comments stay separate
policies.basis: D33 (product owner, 28 Sep 2026) accepted the platforms' terms-of-service risk for public videos and captions (yt-dlp, youtube-transcript-api) and local transcription with faster-whisper, settling I05. Version 2 applies it at Step 06 (D47). Retention follows the youtube family (30 days). Quotation follows D28: spoken reviews in the speaker's words with a credit line. Version 3 (product owner, 1 Oct 2026, Z3): frames and on-screen text are analysed too (D49).

conditions: Quote only registry facts (IDs, dates, registered names, status) together with the record date
robots.txt is asked for every page and its verdict recorded; it does not block the fetch (D46)
policies.basis: Public regulatory records used as dated primary evidence. Version 2 (product owner, 1 Oct 2026, D46): robots.txt is recorded, not enforced. Pages that refuse our crawler are still not worked around (D33).

conditions: Public posts and reels only, found by Brave Search and linked to a catalogue project
Read through Scrapfly with its unblocker and residential proxy pool (D54); no sign-in, accounts, cookies or private content
Caption, the author's username and the post time only; no profile data; comments are not read in this version
A page gated for logged-out visitors is recorded and skipped
robots.txt is asked for every page and its verdict recorded; it does not block the fetch
Quoted captions are re-checked on refresh and withdrawn if the post is removed
policies.basis: D54 (product owner, 9 Oct 2026: 'we should do this'): the product owner accepts Instagram's terms-of-service risk and Scrapfly's anti-bot handling and residential proxies for public posts. Retention as for YouTube (30 days). Quotation follows D28: a caption is a first-person post shown with a credit line. robots.txt is recorded, not enforced, as for official_records (D46); instagram.com's robots.txt disallows unlisted crawlers, so enforcing it would read nothing.

D56 (product owner, 13 Oct 2026: 'Build the Google Alerts with RSS delivery'): Google Alerts RSS as the free listening source. google.com's robots.txt disallows /alerts/ for crawlers; reading one's own subscribed feeds is feed-reader use, so robots.txt is recorded, not enforced (as D46). Version 2 (D59, 13 Oct 2026): withdrawn by the product owner; Google Alerts overlaps Brave Search, so nothing is collected under this family.
